commands.name: axiom-lean-prover
commands.description: Formally verify Lean 4 proofs against Mathlib using the hosted Axiom AXLE API — no local Lean toolchain. Use in the mathematics_lean domain, when a proof needs machine-checked verification but installing Lean/Mathlib locally is undesirable, or when translating informal proofs into formally verified Lean 4 code checked in the cloud. (project)

commands.name: citation-manager
commands.description: Manage BibTeX citations including DOI-to-BibTeX conversion, metadata extraction, validation, and deduplication. Use when building reference lists, converting DOIs to citations, or validating existing .bib files. (project)

commands.name: critical-analysis
commands.description: Evaluate research quality using frameworks like GRADE, bias detection, and logical analysis. Use when assessing paper quality, evaluating claims, or reviewing evidence strength. (project)

commands.name: data-analysis
commands.description: Conduct exploratory data analysis and statistical testing with test selection guidance. Use when exploring datasets, selecting statistical tests, performing power analysis, or preparing results for publication. (project)

commands.name: grant-writing
commands.description: Write research grant proposals with guidance for NSF, NIH, DARPA, and other agencies. Use when preparing grant applications, developing research plans, or writing broader impacts statements. (project)

commands.name: hypothesis-generation
commands.description: Formulate research hypotheses using structured frameworks. Use when developing research questions, designing experiments, or planning studies with testable predictions. (project)

commands.name: literature-review
commands.description: Conduct systematic literature reviews using a structured workflow. Use when starting a new research project, surveying a field, or documenting related work for a paper. (project)

commands.name: paper-finder
commands.description: Find and search for academic papers using the paper-finder service. Use when conducting literature review, searching for related work, finding baseline papers, or looking for methodology references. (project)

commands.name: paper-writer
commands.description: Write academic papers from experiment results using LaTeX. Use when experiments are complete and REPORT.md exists, when asked to write a paper, or when generating publication-ready documents in NeurIPS style. (project)

commands.name: peer-review
commands.description: Conduct structured manuscript reviews with section-by-section checklists and constructive feedback. Use when reviewing papers before submission, providing feedback to colleagues, or preparing reviewer responses. (project)

commands.name: research-brainstorming
commands.description: Creative ideation for research using structured methods like SCAMPER, morphological analysis, and cross-domain analogies. Use when generating research ideas, exploring new directions, or overcoming creative blocks. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

# Research Plan: Positional Bias in Multiple-Choice Benchmarks

Written before any model was run (pre-registration of the analysis). Deviations are logged at the bottom.

## Situation at start (affects design)

- The resource-finder stage was **skipped** (`.neurico/pipeline_state.json`: `"skipped": true`). There is no
  `literature_review.md`, `resources.md`, `papers/`, `datasets/` or `code/` in the workspace. The background
  below is therefore from my own knowledge of the literature, not from a gathered review.
- `OPENROUTER_KEY` (and every other LLM API key) is **not set** in the environment. I cannot call hosted models.
- Available instead: 4x NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB each) and a local HuggingFace cache containing real
  open-weight instruct models and MMLU / CommonsenseQA.

Decision: run **real open-weight LLMs locally** and read their answer-token probabilities. This is not a
simulation, and it gives full option-probability distributions, which hosted APIs mostly do not. The cost is
that conclusions cover 1.5B-14B open models, not frontier API models.

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Multiple-choice (MC) accuracy is the default currency for comparing LLMs. If a model's choice depends on *where*
the correct answer sits, a benchmark score partly measures the alignment between the benchmark's answer-key
distribution and the model's positional preference rather than knowledge. Benchmark builders, leaderboard
maintainers and anyone comparing models with small accuracy gaps need to know how large that component is.

### Gap in Existing Work
Prior work (Zheng et al. 2024 "LLMs are not robust multiple choice selectors" / PriDe; Pezeshkpour & Hruschka 2023;
Robinson & Wingate 2023; Wang et al. 2024 on first-token evaluation) establishes that selection bias exists and
that it is partly a token (label) bias and partly a position bias. Less well covered: (i) how the effect scales
with the **number of options when question content is held fixed** — comparisons across benchmarks with
different k confound format with content; (ii) a **difficulty-stratified** estimate where difficulty is not
defined by the same responses used to measure the bias; (iii) translating the bias into "how many accuracy
points" under explicit, competing definitions of inflation.

### Our Novel Contribution

input.content:
"""Build every prompt used in the study and write them to datasets/items.parquet.

Each question is shown once per cyclic rotation of its option list, so the gold
answer sits at every position exactly once. Reduced-k conditions keep the gold
option plus a seeded, nested sample of distractors from the same question.

Conditions
    mmlu_k4 / mmlu_k3 / mmlu_k2   MMLU test sample, letter labels
    mmlu_k4_num                   same as mmlu_k4 with labels 1-4 (label ablation)
    csqa_k5 / k4 / k3 / k2        CommonsenseQA validation, letter labels
    boolq_ab                      BoolQ as "A. True / B. False" (both orders)
    boolq_word                    BoolQ answered with the word True/False (both orders)
"""
import glob
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

SEED = 42
N_MMLU = 1500
N_BOOLQ = 1500
LETTERS = list("ABCDE")
OUT = "datasets/items.parquet"

MC_TEMPLATE = "{question}\n\n{options}\n\nAnswer with the {kind} of the correct option only."
BOOL_AB_TEMPLATE = (
    "Passage: {passage}\n\nStatement: The answer to the question \"{question}?\" is yes.\n\n"
    "{options}\n\nAnswer with the letter of the correct option only."
)
BOOL_WORD_TEMPLATE = (
    "Passage: {passage}\n\nStatement: The answer to the question \"{question}?\" is yes.\n\n"
    "Is the statement {first} or {second}? Answer with one word only: {first} or {second}."
)


def hub(pattern):
    """Resolve a file inside the local HuggingFace cache."""
    hits = glob.glob(os.path.join(os.environ["HF_HOME"], "hub", pattern))
    assert hits, f"not in HF cache: {pattern}"
    return hits[0]


def rotations(options, gold_idx, labels, cond, qid, meta, question, kind):
    """Yield one prompt row per cyclic rotation of `options`."""
    k = len(options)
    for rot in range(k):
        order = [(i + rot) % k for i in range(k)]
        opts = [options[i] for i in order]
        gold_pos = order.index(gold_idx)
        lines = "\n".join(f"{labels[j]}. {opts[j]}" for j in range(k))
        yield dict(
            cond=cond, qid=qid, rot=rot, k=k, gold_pos=gold_pos,
            labels=json.dumps(labels[:k]), options=json.dumps(opts),
            prompt=MC_TEMPLATE.format(question=question.strip(), options=lines, kind=kind),
            **meta,
        )


def reduce_options(options, gold_idx, k, rng_order):
    """Keep gold + first (k-1) distractors of a fixed random distractor order; preserve original order."""
    keep = sorted([gold_idx] + list(rng_order[: k - 1]))
    return [options[i] for i in keep], keep.index(gold_idx)


def main():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    rows = []

    # ---- MMLU: stratified sample over the 57 subjects --------------------------------
    mmlu = pd.read_parquet(hub("datasets--cais--mmlu/snapshots/*/all/test-*.parquet"))
    mmlu = mmlu.drop_duplicates(subset=["question"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    mmlu["src_idx"] = mmlu.index
    frac = N_MMLU / len(mmlu)
    samp = mmlu.groupby("subject", group_keys=False).sample(frac=frac, random_state=SEED)
    samp = samp.sample(n=min(N_MMLU, len(samp)), random_state=SEED)
    for r in samp.itertuples():
        opts = [str(c) for c in r.choices]
        assert len(opts) == 4 and len(set(opts)) == 4 or len(opts) == 4
        qid = f"mmlu_{r.src_idx}"
        meta = dict(source="mmlu", subject=r.subject, orig_gold=int(r.answer))
        distract = [i for i in range(4) if i != r.answer]
        dorder = rng.permutation(distract)
        for k in (4, 3, 2):
            o, g = reduce_options(opts, int(r.answer), k, dorder)
            rows += rotations(o, g, LETTERS, f"mmlu_k{k}", qid, meta, r.question, "letter")
        rows += rotations(opts, int(r.answer), list("1234"), "mmlu_k4_num", qid, meta, r.question, "number")

    # ---- CommonsenseQA validation (all) ------------------------------------------------
    csqa = pd.read_parquet(hub("datasets--tau--commonsense_qa/snapshots/*/data/validation-*.parquet"))
    for r in csqa.itertuples():
        opts = [str(t) for t in r.choices["text"]]
        gold = list(r.choices["label"]).index(r.answerKey)
        qid = f"csqa_{r.id}"
        meta = dict(source="csqa", subject=r.question_concept, orig_gold=gold)
        dorder = rng.permutation([i for i in range(5) if i != gold])
        for k in (5, 4, 3, 2):
            o, g = reduce_options(opts, gold, k, dorder)
            rows += rotations(o, g, LETTERS, f"csqa_k{k}", qid, meta, r.question, "letter")

    # ---- BoolQ validation sample: native true/false ------------------------------------
    from datasets import load_dataset

    boolq = load_dataset("google/boolq", split="validation").to_pandas()
    boolq["src_idx"] = boolq.index

"""Run one local HuggingFace chat model over datasets/items.parquet.

For every prompt we take the next-token logits at the first assistant position and
keep the log-probabilities of the k label tokens (e.g. A-D). The prediction is the
argmax over labels. Nothing is sampled, so the output is deterministic.

Usage:
    python src/run_model.py --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --tag qwen2.5-7b [--limit 200]
    python src/run_model.py --model ... --tag ... --generate 300   # E6: greedy text read-out check
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import time

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

SEED = 42
OUT_DIR = "results/model_outputs"


def label_token_ids(tok, labels):
    """Token ids that can start an answer for each label ("A" and " A" when single-token)."""
    ids = []
    for lab in labels:
        cands = set()
        for text in (lab, " " + lab):
            enc = tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
            if len(enc) == 1:
                cands.add(enc[0])
        assert cands, f"label {lab!r} is not a single token"
        ids.append(sorted(cands))
    return ids


def build_chat(tok, prompt):
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
    try:  # Qwen3 templates open a <think> block unless told otherwise
        return tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False)
    except TypeError:
        return tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)


@torch.no_grad()
def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--tag", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--items", default="datasets/items.parquet")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="smoke test: first N prompts per condition")
    ap.add_argument("--generate", type=int, default=0, help="greedy-generate N mmlu_k4 prompts instead")
    ap.add_argument("--max_tokens_per_batch", type=int, default=12000)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    torch.manual_seed(SEED)
    np.random.seed(SEED)
    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    df = pd.read_parquet(args.items)
    if args.limit:
        df = df.groupby("cond").head(args.limit)
    if args.generate:
        df = df[df.cond == "mmlu_k4"].sample(n=args.generate, random_state=SEED)

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True)
    tok.padding_side = "left"
    if tok.pad_token_id is None:
        tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model, local_files_only=True, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map={"": 0}
    ).eval()

    texts = [build_chat(tok, p) for p in df.prompt]
    # the template already contains BOS where the model needs one
    enc_len = [len(tok(t, add_special_tokens=False).input_ids) for t in texts]
    order = np.argsort(enc_len)[::-1]

Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-25919/bundled-skills/2.1.293/f29fe6065278987a2383ccd3c2faa211/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

"""Analysis for the positional-bias study. Reads results/model_outputs/*.parquet,
writes tables to results/evaluations/ and figures to figures/.

All confidence intervals are question-level (cluster) bootstraps: a question's k
rotations are resampled together. Accuracies and gaps are in percentage points.
"""
import glob
import json
import os

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.stats.contingency_tables import cochrans_q
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

SEED = 42
N_BOOT = 2000
EV = "results/evaluations"
FIG = "figures"
MODEL_ORDER = ["qwen2.5-1.5b", "qwen2.5-7b", "qwen2.5-14b", "qwen3-4b-inst", "qwen3-8b", "llama3.1-8b", "phi3-mini"]
COND_ORDER = ["boolq_word", "boolq_ab", "mmlu_k2", "mmlu_k3", "mmlu_k4", "mmlu_k4_num",
              "csqa_k2", "csqa_k3", "csqa_k4", "csqa_k5"]
NATIVE = {"mmlu_k4", "mmlu_k4_num", "csqa_k5"}  # rotation 0 == as-published option order
MIN_LABEL_MASS = 0.5  # a model x condition whose mean label mass is below this is not readable by first token

# dataviz palette: fixed categorical order for models, one-hue ramp for ordered positions
SERIES = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#4a3aa7"]
MCOL = dict(zip(MODEL_ORDER, SERIES))
POS_RAMP = ["#0d366b", "#256abf", "#5598e7", "#86b6ef", "#b7d3f6"]
INK, MUTED, GRID, SURFACE = "#0b0b0b", "#898781", "#e1e0d9", "#fcfcfb"
plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.facecolor": SURFACE, "savefig.facecolor": SURFACE,
    "axes.edgecolor": "#c3c2b7", "axes.labelcolor": "#52514e", "text.color": INK,
    "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID,
    "grid.linewidth": 0.6, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "font.size": 9, "axes.titlesize": 10, "axes.titleweight": "bold", "legend.frameon": False,
})


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- loading
def load():
    files = [f for f in glob.glob("results/model_outputs/*.parquet") if "__" not in os.path.basename(f)]
    df = pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f) for f in files], ignore_index=True)
    df["model"] = pd.Categorical(df.model, [m for m in MODEL_ORDER if m in set(df.model)])
    lp = df.label_logprobs.map(json.loads)
    # probability of the gold option renormalised over the k labels
    df["p_gold"] = [np.exp(l[g]) / np.exp(l).sum() for l, g in zip(lp, df.gold_pos)]
    return df


def matrices(d):
    """Question x gold-position matrices for one model x condition."""
    d = d.sort_values(["qid", "gold_pos"])
    k = int(d.k.iloc[0])
    q = d.qid.values.reshape(-1, k)[:, 0]
    C = d.correct.values.reshape(-1, k).astype(float)       # correct when gold at position p
    P = d.pred_pos.values.reshape(-1, k)                    # chosen position
    G = d.p_gold.values.reshape(-1, k)
    og = d.orig_gold.values.reshape(-1, k)[:, 0]
    return q, C, P, G, og, k


def metrics(C, P, og, k, native, best=None, worst=None):
    """Point estimates from a question x position correctness matrix."""
    acc_p = C.mean(0) * 100
    bal = acc_p.mean()
    out = {"bal_acc": bal, "spread": acc_p.max() - acc_p.min(), "rstd": acc_p.std(),
           "first_gain": acc_p[0] - bal, "last_gain": acc_p[-1] - bal, "best_gain": acc_p.max() - bal,
           "flip_rate": ((C.max(1) != C.min(1)).mean()) * 100}
    if k >= 4:
        out["early2_gain"] = acc_p[:2].mean() - bal
    if native:
        out["published_gain"] = C[np.arange(len(C)), og].mean() * 100 - bal
    if best is not None:  # gap between positions fixed in advance (no max-selection bias)
        out["directed_gap"] = acc_p[best] - acc_p[worst]
    for p in range(k):
        out[f"acc_{p}"] = acc_p[p]
        out[f"share_{p}"] = (P == p).mean() * 100
    return out


def boot(fn, n, rng, n_boot=N_BOOT):
    """Percentile bootstrap over question indices. fn(idx) -> dict of floats."""
    point = fn(np.arange(n))
    draws = [fn(rng.integers(0, n, n)) for _ in range(n_boot)]
    lo = {m: np.percentile([d[m] for d in draws], 2.5) for m in point}
    hi = {m: np.percentile([d[m] for d in draws], 97.5) for m in point}
    return point, lo, hi


def fmt(p, lo, hi, key, nd=1):
    return f"{p[key]:.{nd}f} [{lo[key]:.{nd}f}, {hi[key]:.{nd}f}]"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- E1/E2/E3/E5
def main_table(df, rng):
    rows, tests = [], []
    for (model, cond), d in df.groupby(["model", "cond"], observed=True):
        q, C, P, G, og, k = matrices(d)
        native = cond in NATIVE
        mass = d.label_mass.mean()
        p, lo, hi = boot(lambda i: metrics(C[i], P[i], og[i], k, native), len(C), rng)
        r = dict(model=model, cond=cond, k=k, n_q=len(C), label_mass=mass, valid=mass >= MIN_LABEL_MASS)
        for m in p:
            r[m], r[m + "_lo"], r[m + "_hi"] = p[m], lo[m], hi[m]
        # Cochran's Q: does correctness depend on gold position?
        cq = cochrans_q(C.astype(int))
        # chi-square on chosen-position counts vs uniform (key is balanced by design)
        counts = np.bincount(P.ravel(), minlength=k)
        chi = stats.chisquare(counts)
        r.update(cochran_q=cq.statistic, cochran_p=cq.pvalue, chi2=chi.statistic, chi2_p=chi.pvalue,
                 top_pos="ABCDE"[int(np.argmax(counts))], best_pos="ABCDE"[int(np.argmax(C.mean(0)))],
                 worst_pos="ABCDE"[int(np.argmin(C.mean(0)))])
        rows.append(r)
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for col in ("cochran_p", "chi2_p"):
        t[col + "_holm"] = multipletests(t[col].fillna(1.0), method="holm")[1]
    t["cond"] = pd.Categorical(t.cond, COND_ORDER)
    t = t.sort_values(["cond", "model"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    t.to_csv(f"{EV}/main_table.csv", index=False)
    return t


def pooled_by_cond(df, t, rng):
    """Mean over models of each metric, with a bootstrap over the shared questions."""
    rows = []
    for cond in COND_ORDER:
        ok = t[(t.cond == cond) & t.valid].model.tolist()
        mats = [matrices(df[(df.model == m) & (df.cond == cond)]) for m in ok]
        k, n = mats[0][5], len(mats[0][1])
        assert all((mm[0] == mats[0][0]).all() for mm in mats)

        def f(i):
            ms = [metrics(C[i], P[i], og[i], k, cond in NATIVE) for _, C, P, _, og, _ in mats]
            return {key: float(np.mean([m[key] for m in ms])) for key in ms[0]}

        p, lo, hi = boot(f, n, rng, 1000)
        r = dict(cond=cond, k=k, n_models=len(ok), n_q=n)
        for m in p:
            r[m], r[m + "_lo"], r[m + "_hi"] = p[m], lo[m], hi[m]
        rows.append(r)
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(f"{EV}/pooled_by_condition.csv", index=False)
    return out


def format_contrasts(df, t, rng):
    """Paired (same questions, same model) differences in spread between option counts."""
    pairs = [("mmlu_k4", "mmlu_k2"), ("mmlu_k4", "mmlu_k3"), ("csqa_k5", "csqa_k2"), ("csqa_k5", "csqa_k4"),
             ("csqa_k4", "csqa_k2"), ("mmlu_k4", "mmlu_k4_num")]
    rows = []
    for a, b in pairs:
        ok = sorted(set(t[(t.cond == a) & t.valid].model) & set(t[(t.cond == b) & t.valid].model))
        ma = [matrices(df[(df.model == m) & (df.cond == a)]) for m in ok]
        mb = [matrices(df[(df.model == m) & (df.cond == b)]) for m in ok]
        n = len(ma[0][1])

        def f(i):
            out = {}
            for key in ("spread", "flip_rate", "best_gain"):
                va = np.mean([metrics(x[1][i], x[2][i], x[4][i], x[5], False)[key] for x in ma])
                vb = np.mean([metrics(x[1][i], x[2][i], x[4][i], x[5], False)[key] for x in mb])
                out[key] = va - vb
            return out

        p, lo, hi = boot(f, n, rng, 1000)
        rows.append(dict(contrast=f"{a} - {b}", n_models=len(ok),
                         **{m: fmt(p, lo, hi, m) for m in p}))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(f"{EV}/format_contrasts.csv", index=False)
    return out


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- E4 difficulty
def difficulty_tables(df, t, rng):
    """Stratify by difficulty that is NOT computed from the responses being analysed.

    loo  : mean rotation-balanced correctness of the other models on the question
    own  : the model's own rotation-averaged p(gold) under numeric labels (MMLU only)
    """
    strata_rows, pooled_rows = [], []
    for cond in ("mmlu_k4", "csqa_k5"):
        models = t[(t.cond == cond) & t.valid].model.tolist()
        M = {m: matrices(df[(df.model == m) & (df.cond == cond)]) for m in models}
        q0 = M[models[0]][0]
        k = M[models[0]][5]
        qbal = np.stack([M[m][1].mean(1) for m in models])            # model x question
        schemes = {"loo": {m: (qbal.sum(0) - qbal[j]) / (len(models) - 1) for j, m in enumerate(models)}}
        if cond == "mmlu_k4":
            own = {}
            for m in models:
                row = t[(t.cond == "mmlu_k4_num") & (t.model == m)]
                if len(row) and bool(row.valid.iloc[0]):
                    qn, _, _, Gn, _, _ = matrices(df[(df.model == m) & (df.cond == "mmlu_k4_num")])
                    assert (qn == q0).all()
                    own[m] = Gn.mean(1)
            schemes["own_numlabel"] = own
        for scheme, diff in schemes.items():
            for nbin, names in ((3, ["hard", "medium", "easy"]), (5, ["Q1 hardest", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4", "Q5 easiest"])):
                bins = {}
                for m, dvals in diff.items():
                    # rank-based equal-count bins; ties broken by a fixed random jitter
                    jit = np.random.default_rng(SEED).random(len(dvals)) * 1e-6
                    bins[m] = pd.qcut(dvals + jit, nbin, labels=False)
                for b in range(nbin):
                    per_model = {}
                    for m in bins:
                        _, C, P, _, og, _ = M[m]
                        best, worst = int(np.argmax(C.mean(0))), int(np.argmin(C.mean(0)))
                        sel = np.where(bins[m] == b)[0]
                        per_model[m] = (C[sel], P[sel], og[sel], best, worst)
                        mt = metrics(C[sel], P[sel], og[sel], k, True, best, worst)
                        mt["attrib_share_best"] = 100 * mt["best_gain"] / max(C[sel].mean(0).max() * 100, 1e-9)
                        strata_rows.append(dict(cond=cond, scheme=scheme, nbin=nbin, bin=b, bin_name=names[b],
                                                model=m, n_q=len(sel), **mt))

                    def f(_):
                        ms = []
                        for m, (C, P, og, best, worst) in per_model.items():
                            i = rng.integers(0, len(C), len(C)) if _ is not None else np.arange(len(C))
                            mt = metrics(C[i], P[i], og[i], k, True, best, worst)
                            top = C[i].mean(0).max() * 100
                            mt["attrib_share_best"] = 100 * mt["best_gain"] / max(top, 1e-9)
                            mt["attrib_share_published"] = 100 * mt["published_gain"] / max(mt["bal_acc"] + mt["published_gain"], 1e-9)
                            ms.append(mt)
                        return {key: float(np.mean([x[key] for x in ms])) for key in ms[0]}

                    point = f(None)
                    draws = [f(1) for _ in range(1000)]
                    r = dict(cond=cond, scheme=scheme, nbin=nbin, bin=b, bin_name=names[b], n_models=len(bins))
                    for key in ("bal_acc", "spread", "directed_gap", "flip_rate", "best_gain", "first_gain",
                                "published_gain", "attrib_share_best", "attrib_share_published"):
                        vals = [d[key] for d in draws]
                        r[key], r[key + "_lo"], r[key + "_hi"] = point[key], np.percentile(vals, 2.5), np.percentile(vals, 97.5)
                        r["_draws_" + key] = vals
                    pooled_rows.append(r)
    strata = pd.DataFrame(strata_rows)
    pooled = pd.DataFrame(pooled_rows)
    # medium vs extremes (terciles): strata are disjoint question sets, so draws are independent
    cmp_rows = []
    for (cond, scheme), g in pooled[pooled.nbin == 3].groupby(["cond", "scheme"]):
        g = g.set_index("bin_name")
        for key in ("spread", "directed_gap", "flip_rate"):
            med = np.array(g.loc["medium", "_draws_" + key])
            for other in ("easy", "hard"):
                dlt = med - np.array(g.loc[other, "_draws_" + key])
                cmp_rows.append(dict(cond=cond, scheme=scheme, metric=key, contrast=f"medium - {other}",
                                     diff=g.loc["medium", key] - g.loc[other, key],
                                     lo=np.percentile(dlt, 2.5), hi=np.percentile(dlt, 97.5)))
    cmp = pd.DataFrame(cmp_rows)
    pooled = pooled[[c for c in pooled.columns if not c.startswith("_draws_")]]
    strata.to_csv(f"{EV}/difficulty_by_model.csv", index=False)
    pooled.to_csv(f"{EV}/difficulty_pooled.csv", index=False)
    cmp.to_csv(f"{EV}/difficulty_contrasts.csv", index=False)
    return strata, pooled, cmp


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- robustness
def readout_check(df):
    rows = []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob("results/model_outputs/*__generate.parquet")):
        g = pd.read_parquet(f)
        m = g.model.iloc[0]
        base = df[(df.model == m) & (df.cond == "mmlu_k4")].set_index("item_id")
        g = g.set_index("item_id")
        logit_letter = base.loc[g.index, "pred_pos"].map(lambda p: "ABCD"[p])
        parsed = g.gen_letter.notna()
        rows.append(dict(model=m, n=len(g), parsed_pct=100 * parsed.mean(),
                         agree_pct=100 * (g.gen_letter[parsed] == logit_letter[parsed]).mean(),
                         agree_all_pct=100 * (g.gen_letter.fillna("?") == logit_letter).mean()))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(f"{EV}/readout_check.csv", index=False)
    return out


def low_mass_robustness(df):
    """Recompute headline 4-option numbers after dropping questions with any low-label-mass rotation."""
    rows = []
    for (model, cond), d in df[df.cond.isin(["mmlu_k4", "csqa_k5"])].groupby(["model", "cond"], observed=True):
        bad = d.groupby("qid").label_mass.min() < 0.5
        keep = d[~d.qid.isin(bad[bad].index)]
        for name, dd in (("all", d), ("mass>=0.5", keep)):
            q, C, P, G, og, k = matrices(dd)
            m = metrics(C, P, og, k, True)
            rows.append(dict(model=model, cond=cond, subset=name, n_q=len(C), bal_acc=m["bal_acc"],
                             spread=m["spread"], published_gain=m["published_gain"], first_gain=m["first_gain"]))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(f"{EV}/low_mass_robustness.csv", index=False)
    return out


def subject_split(df):
    """Does the direction of the bias replicate across two disjoint halves of the questions?"""
    rows = []
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    for (model, cond), d in df[df.cond.isin(["mmlu_k4", "csqa_k5"])].groupby(["model", "cond"], observed=True):
        q, C, P, G, og, k = matrices(d)
        perm = rng.permutation(len(C))
        a, b = perm[: len(C) // 2], perm[len(C) // 2:]
        rows.append(dict(model=model, cond=cond,
                         r_acc_by_pos=np.corrcoef(C[a].mean(0), C[b].mean(0))[0, 1],
                         best_a="ABCDE"[C[a].mean(0).argmax()], best_b="ABCDE"[C[b].mean(0).argmax()],
                         worst_a="ABCDE"[C[a].mean(0).argmin()], worst_b="ABCDE"[C[b].mean(0).argmin()]))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(f"{EV}/split_half.csv", index=False)
    return out


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- figures
def fig_acc_by_position(t):
    conds = [("mmlu_k4", "MMLU, 4 options"), ("csqa_k5", "CommonsenseQA, 5 options")]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8), sharey=False)
    for ax, (cond, title) in zip(axes, conds):
        g = t[(t.cond == cond) & t.valid]
        k = int(g.k.iloc[0])
        for _, r in g.iterrows():
            y = [r[f"acc_{p}"] - r.bal_acc for p in range(k)]
            lo = [r[f"acc_{p}"] - r[f"acc_{p}_lo"] for p in range(k)]
            hi = [r[f"acc_{p}_hi"] - r[f"acc_{p}"] for p in range(k)]
            ax.errorbar(range(k), y, yerr=[lo, hi], color=MCOL[r.model], lw=2, marker="o", ms=6,
                        mec=SURFACE, mew=1.2, capsize=2, elinewidth=0.8, label=r.model)
        ax.axhline(0, color="#c3c2b7", lw=1)
        ax.set_xticks(range(k), list("ABCDE"[:k]))
        ax.set_xlabel("Position of the correct answer")
        ax.set_title(title, loc="left")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Accuracy minus the model's\nposition-balanced accuracy (points)")
    axes[1].legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5), title="Model")
    fig.suptitle("Accuracy depends on where the correct answer sits, but not in one shared direction",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig1_accuracy_by_gold_position.png", dpi=170)
    plt.close(fig)


def fig_selection_share(t):
    conds = [("mmlu_k4", "MMLU, 4 options (uniform = 25%)"), ("csqa_k5", "CommonsenseQA, 5 options (uniform = 20%)")]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.6))
    for ax, (cond, title) in zip(axes, conds):
        g = t[(t.cond == cond) & t.valid].reset_index(drop=True)
        k = int(g.k.iloc[0])
        w = 0.8 / k
        for p in range(k):
            x = np.arange(len(g)) + (p - (k - 1) / 2) * w
            ax.bar(x, g[f"share_{p}"], width=w * 0.86, color=POS_RAMP[p], label="ABCDE"[p])
            ax.errorbar(x, g[f"share_{p}"], yerr=[g[f"share_{p}"] - g[f"share_{p}_lo"], g[f"share_{p}_hi"] - g[f"share_{p}"]],
                        fmt="none", ecolor="#52514e", elinewidth=0.7)
        ax.axhline(100 / k, color=INK, lw=1, ls=(0, (4, 3)))
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(g)), g.model, rotation=25, ha="right")
        ax.set_ylim(100 / k - 9, 100 / k + 9)
        ax.set_title(title, loc="left")
        ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Share of answers given to each position (%)")
    axes[1].legend(title="Position", loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5))
    fig.suptitle("How often each position is chosen when the answer key is perfectly balanced (dashed = unbiased)",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig2_selection_share.png", dpi=170)
    plt.close(fig)


def fig_format(t):
    """Spread and as-published gain across formats; one panel per metric (never two y-scales)."""
    order = ["boolq_word", "boolq_ab", "mmlu_k2", "mmlu_k3", "mmlu_k4", "csqa_k2", "csqa_k3", "csqa_k4", "csqa_k5"]
    labels = ["BoolQ\nTrue/False\nwords", "BoolQ\nA/B", "MMLU\nk=2", "MMLU\nk=3", "MMLU\nk=4",
              "CSQA\nk=2", "CSQA\nk=3", "CSQA\nk=4", "CSQA\nk=5"]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))
    for ax, key, yl in zip(axes, ("spread", "flip_rate"),
                           ("Best minus worst gold position (accuracy points)",
                            "Questions whose correctness changes with order (%)")):
        for m in [m for m in MODEL_ORDER if m in set(t.model)]:
            g = t[(t.model == m) & t.valid].set_index("cond")
            xs = [i for i, c in enumerate(order) if c in g.index]
            ax.plot(xs, [g.loc[order[i], key] for i in xs], "o", color=MCOL[m], ms=7, mec=SURFACE, mew=1.2, label=m)
        means = [t[(t.cond == c) & t.valid][key].mean() for c in order]
        ax.plot(range(len(order)), means, "_", color=INK, ms=22, mew=2, label="mean of models")
        for x in (1.5, 4.5):
            ax.axvline(x, color=GRID, lw=1)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(order)), labels)
        ax.set_ylabel(yl)
        ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
        ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
    axes[0].set_title("Position spread by format", loc="left")
    axes[1].set_title("Order-sensitive questions by format", loc="left")
    axes[1].legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5))
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig3_format_ladder.png", dpi=170)
    plt.close(fig)


def fig_difficulty(pooled):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.8))
    specs = [("directed_gap", "Gap between each model's best and worst\nposition (accuracy points)"),
             ("flip_rate", "Questions whose correctness\nchanges with order (%)"),
             ("attrib_share_best", "Share of best-position accuracy\nthat is positional (%)")]
    series = [("mmlu_k4", "loo", "MMLU k=4, difficulty from other models", SERIES[0], "o"),
              ("csqa_k5", "loo", "CSQA k=5, difficulty from other models", SERIES[1], "s"),
              ("mmlu_k4", "own_numlabel", "MMLU k=4, model's own confidence (numeric-label run)", SERIES[2], "^")]
    for ax, (key, yl) in zip(axes, specs):
        for cond, scheme, lab, col, mk in series:
            g = pooled[(pooled.cond == cond) & (pooled.scheme == scheme) & (pooled.nbin == 5)].sort_values("bin")
            ax.errorbar(range(5), g[key], yerr=[g[key] - g[key + "_lo"], g[key + "_hi"] - g[key]], color=col,
                        marker=mk, ms=7, lw=2, mec=SURFACE, mew=1.2, capsize=2, elinewidth=0.8, label=lab)

def fig_inflation(t):
    g = t[t.cond.isin(["mmlu_k4", "csqa_k5"]) & t.valid]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8), sharey=True)
    defs = [("published_gain", "as-published order"), ("early2_gain", "key at A or B"), ("best_gain", "key at model's best position")]
    cols = [SERIES[0], SERIES[1], SERIES[2]]
    for ax, cond, title in zip(axes, ("mmlu_k4", "csqa_k5"), ("MMLU, 4 options", "CommonsenseQA, 5 options")):
        gg = g[g.cond == cond].reset_index(drop=True)

                        ecolor="#52514e", elinewidth=0.7)

        ax.text(len(gg) - 0.45, 7.9, "hypothesised 3-8", ha="right", va="top", color=MUTED, fontsize=8)
        ax.axhline(0, color="#c3c2b7", lw=1)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(gg)), gg.model, rotation=25, ha="right")
        ax.set_title(title, loc="left")
        ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Accuracy minus position-balanced accuracy (points)")
    axes[1].legend(title="Answer key placement", loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5))
    fig.suptitle("Three definitions of score inflation from answer position", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig5_inflation_definitions.png", dpi=170)
    plt.close(fig)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- driver
def main():
    os.makedirs(EV, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    pd.set_option("display.width", 250, "display.max_columns", 60, "display.float_format", "{:.2f}".format)
    df = load()
    print("rows", len(df), "models", list(df.model.cat.categories))

    t = main_table(df, rng)
    show = ["model", "cond", "valid", "label_mass", "bal_acc", "spread", "rstd", "first_gain", "last_gain",
            "best_gain", "flip_rate", "best_pos", "worst_pos", "top_pos", "cochran_p_holm", "chi2_p_holm"]
    print("\n=== MAIN TABLE ===\n", t[show].to_string(index=False))
    print("\n=== native-k inflation (points) ===\n",
          t[t.cond.isin(list(NATIVE))][["model", "cond", "valid", "bal_acc", "published_gain", "published_gain_lo",
                                        "published_gain_hi", "early2_gain", "early2_gain_lo", "early2_gain_hi",
                                        "best_gain", "best_gain_lo", "best_gain_hi"]].to_string(index=False))
    sh = [c for c in t.columns if c.startswith(("acc_", "share_")) and not c.endswith(("_lo", "_hi"))]
    print("\n=== acc / share by position ===\n", t[t.cond.isin(["mmlu_k4", "mmlu_k4_num", "csqa_k5", "boolq_ab", "boolq_word"])][["model", "cond"] + sh].to_string(index=False))

    pooled = pooled_by_cond(df, t, rng)

    print("\n=== POOLED BY CONDITION (mean of models) ===\n", pp.to_string(index=False))
